stories.headline: OpenAI says two API settings tripled GPT-5.6 Sol's ARC-AGI-3 score; ARC Prize pushes back

key_facts.fact: In a July 29 post, OpenAI said turning on two API settings it already uses in ChatGPT and Codex — retained reasoning and compaction — tripled GPT-5.6 Sol's ARC-AGI-3 score on the public task set and cut output tokens by 6x
key_facts.excerpt: In the case of ARC-AGI-3, we discovered that turning on two API settings we use in ChatGPT and Codex—retained reasoning and compaction—tripled scores and cut output tokens by 6x on the public task set.

key_facts.fact: With the official ARC-AGI-3 harness GPT-5.6 Sol scored 13.3% on the public set; reimplemented on OpenAI's Responses API with retained reasoning and compaction it scored 38.3%, using roughly six times fewer output tokens per game
key_facts.excerpt: With the official ARC-AGI-3 harness, GPT-5.6 Sol scored 13.3% on the public task set. Using OpenAI's Responses API with retained reasoning and compaction turned on, the same model scored 38.3%, while using roughly six times fewer output tokens per game.

key_facts.fact: The 38.3% figure would beat Anthropic's Claude Opus 5 at 30.2%; in ARC's official harness GPT-5.6 Sol had scored just 7.8% because reasoning is discarded after each action
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI is now showing that GPT-5.6 Sol hits 38.3 percent with two API settings, beating Opus 5's 30.2 percent... In the official harness, GPT-5.6 Sol scored just 7.8 percent because the model's reasoning gets discarded after each action.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI blamed the generic harness: private reasoning was thrown away after every action, and rolling truncation dropped the oldest context once the conversation passed 175,000 characters
key_facts.excerpt: After every action the agent took, its private reasoning was thrown away... the harness used rolling truncation, discarding the oldest parts of the conversation once it grew past 175,000 characters

key_facts.fact: ARC Prize called the finding 'a real and useful result' but said its verified scores deliberately use a 'no harness' approach with client-side conversation state so all providers are compared under the same observations, prompt and action limits
key_facts.excerpt: ARC's verified scores use a "no harness" approach to avoid accidental or intentional developer-aware targeting and to fairly compare scores across all providers... Conversation state is managed client-side using the industry-wide standard interface for LLMs (the OpenAI-style completions API).

key_facts.fact: ARC Prize said it is working with several industry labs, including OpenAI, on how to incorporate server-side state management into its verified testing setup
key_facts.excerpt: we're actively working with several industry labs, including OpenAI, to figure out how to best incorporate these server-side state management findings into our verified testing setup while remaining fair and consistent across providers.

stories.headline: Microsoft says 365 Copilot passed 30M paid seats and Azure topped $100B in a year

key_facts.fact: Satya Nadella said Azure revenue surpassed $100 billion for the first time in fiscal 2026 and that Microsoft 365 Copilot reached over 30 million paid seats
key_facts.excerpt: "This year, Azure revenue surpassed $100 billion for the first time, and Microsoft 365 Copilot reached over 30 million paid seats, reflecting the confidence customers are placing in us to power their AI transformation."

key_facts.fact: Azure and other cloud services revenue grew 43% year over year in the June quarter, and Intelligent Cloud revenue was $39.3 billion, up 32%; commercial remaining performance obligation rose 84%
key_facts.excerpt: Revenue in Intelligent Cloud was $39.3 billion and increased 32%... Azure and other cloud services revenue increased 43%... Commercial remaining performance obligation | 84%

key_facts.fact: On the earnings call Microsoft said net paid Copilot seat adds more than doubled quarter over quarter, and that Azure results benefited from stronger-than-expected GitHub Copilot consumption after a June pricing change tied to usage
key_facts.excerpt: net paid seat adds more than doubled sequentially, with paid seats now over 30 million... Results also benefited from stronger-than-expected GitHub Copilot consumption following the June business model change to align pricing with usage and value.

key_facts.fact: Microsoft guided to roughly 45% Azure growth in constant currency for the September quarter and said customer demand continues to exceed available capacity
key_facts.excerpt: In Azure, we expect revenue growth of approximately 45% in constant currency... Customer demand continues to exceed available capacity.

key_facts.fact: The quarter included a $3.2 billion gain on Microsoft's Anthropic stake, adding 33 cents to diluted EPS, while its OpenAI stake was marked down about $600 million, cutting EPS by about 7 cents
key_facts.excerpt: For the quarter, it recorded its investment in Anthropic as a $3.2 billion gain, boosting diluted earnings per share by 33 cents... marked it down about $600 million, reducing diluted EPS by about 7 cents per share.

key_facts.fact: For the full fiscal year Microsoft's OpenAI investment generated a $5 billion gain and added $0.67 to EPS; quarterly revenue was $90 billion with net income of $35.8 billion
key_facts.excerpt: For the year, Microsoft's OpenAI investment generated a $5 billion gain and added $0.67 on EPS... reporting $90 billion of revenue and net income of $35.8 billion for the quarter.

key_facts.fact: Copilot added roughly 10 million paid seats in a single quarter, and Azure's 43% growth accelerated from 40% in the prior quarter, beating consensus of about 40%
key_facts.excerpt: Microsoft 365 Copilot added roughly 10 million paid seats in a single quarter, bringing the total to over 30 million... Azure's growth rate of 43% year-over-year in the fiscal fourth quarter — accelerating from 40% in the prior quarter — cleared the analyst consensus of approximately 40%

stories.headline: OpenAI CFO tells staff July annualized revenue topped all of the second quarter

key_facts.fact: At an internal meeting on Wednesday, July 29, CFO Sarah Friar told employees that OpenAI's annualized recurring revenue in July exceeded the entire second quarter, adding 'And Q2 was no slouch'
key_facts.excerpt: Friar said OpenAI's annualized recurring revenue in July exceeded the entire second quarter. "And Q2 was no slouch," Friar said, according to a partial transcript of the meeting that was reviewed by CNBC.

key_facts.fact: Board chair Bret Taylor joined Friar at the meeting; both credited growth to the GPT-5.6 model series, the ChatGPT Work enterprise agent and rising adoption of the Codex coding tool
key_facts.excerpt: Alongside Friar, OpenAI's board chair, Bret Taylor, attributed the momentum to the launch of the GPT-5.6 series models, the company's enterprise AI agent ChatGPT Work, and growing adoption of its artificial intelligence (AI) coding tool, Codex.

key_facts.fact: The message was aimed at reassuring employees that the business is healthy as competition intensifies from Anthropic and cheaper open-weight models
key_facts.excerpt: The company is trying to reassure employees that the business is healthy as competition ramps up from Anthropic and a slew of open-source players.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI did not disclose absolute figures; The Information previously reported its annualized revenue topped $25 billion at the end of February

stories.headline: Lilian Weng leaves Thinking Machines and rejoins OpenAI to work on recursive self-improvement

key_facts.fact: OpenAI confirmed on Wednesday, July 29, that Thinking Machines co-founder Lilian Weng is rejoining the company, where she previously served as VP of AI Safety Research
key_facts.excerpt: On Wednesday, OpenAI told TechCrunch that Weng would be rejoining the company, where she previously served as the VP of AI Safety Research.

key_facts.fact: According to an OpenAI spokesperson, Weng will lead a top-level team focused on accelerating internal research, supporting cross-research work on recursive self-improvement — an AI system iterating on itself to become more powerful
key_facts.excerpt: Weng will lead a top-level team focused on accelerating OpenAI's internal research. This team will support cross-research work on recursive self-improvement, a process that would allow an AI system to iterate on itself to become more powerful.

key_facts.fact: Weng announced her exit days earlier citing health, writing 'I don't feel I'm able to continue at the pace a startup requires' and that stress and workload had pushed her beyond what her health could sustain
key_facts.excerpt: "I don't feel I'm able to continue at the pace a startup requires," she wrote in an internal Slack message, which she also shared on X.

key_facts.fact: Weng said July 29 would be her last day at Thinking Machines; she is the third Thinking Machines co-founder to return to OpenAI in 2026, after Barret Zoph and Luke Metz in January
key_facts.excerpt: She cited the health toll of startup work... and said July 29th would be her final day... In January, Thinking Machines Lab cofounders Barret Zoph and Luke Metz returned to OpenAI, alongside researcher Sam Schoenholz. Weng is the third Thinking Machines Lab cofounder to make that trip back in 2026.

key_facts.fact: Her departure came as Thinking Machines was sprinting to ship Inkling, its first open-weight model; by May, 13 of the lab's 42 founding members had left, including three of its six co-founders
key_facts.excerpt: She said she tried to rest while the lab sprinted to ship Inkling, its first open-weight model, but felt guilt... By May, 13 of the lab's 42 founding members had left, including three of its six co-founders, as Meta and OpenAI dangled huge pay packages.

key_facts.fact: Thinking Machines CEO Mira Murati replied publicly to Weng's post: 'We'll miss you, it's been wonderful building Thinky together. I'm glad that you're putting your health first.'
key_facts.excerpt: "We'll miss you, it's been wonderful building Thinky together. I'm glad that you're putting your health first. Thank you for everything," Murati wrote in response to Weng's post.

stories.headline: EU set to put ChatGPT under its strictest platform rules as a 'very large online platform'

key_facts.fact: The European Commission will designate OpenAI's ChatGPT and Roblox as 'very large online platforms' under the Digital Services Act after both passed 45 million monthly users in the bloc, with the move set to come as soon as August
key_facts.excerpt: The EU's executive arm will designate the two US technology companies as "very large online platforms" (VLOPs) in line with the Digital Services Act (DSA), a person familiar with the matter said. The designation is set to come as soon as August

key_facts.fact: VLOPs must file transparency reports, detail risk mitigation plans and pay an annual fee to the Commission; breaches carry fines of up to 6% of annual global sales
key_facts.excerpt: The "VLOPs"... must also file transparency reports, detail risk mitigation plans and pay an annual fee to the European Commission. Companies that breach the DSA risk fines of as much as 6 per cent of their annual global sales.

key_facts.fact: Within four months of designation the companies must set up a contact point for authorities and users, publish user-friendly terms, and be transparent about advertising, recommendation systems and content moderation decisions
key_facts.excerpt: Within four months of being officially designation as a VLOP, they will have to establish a point of contact for authorities and users, launch user-friendly terms and conditions, as well as be transparent when it comes to their advertising, recommendation systems and content moderation decisions.

key_facts.fact: Designated platforms must run annual audits, share data with the Commission and give vetted researchers access, and assess systemic risks including illegal content and electoral processes
key_facts.excerpt: VLOPs are required to establish an internal compliance process, be audited every year... share their data with the European Commission and allow vetted researchers to access it, as well.

key_facts.fact: ChatGPT crossed 120 million monthly users in Europe last year; 21 platforms including X, Amazon, Apple, Microsoft, LinkedIn and TikTok are already subject to the rules
key_facts.excerpt: 21 platforms in the bloc, including X, Amazon, Apple, Microsoft, LinkedIn and TikTok, are already subject to these regulations since the DSA's enforcement in early 2024... ChatGPT crossed 120m monthly users in Europe last year.

stories.headline: Google launches Lyria 3.5 music model in Flow Music with better vocals and tempo control

key_facts.fact: Google announced Lyria 3.5 on July 29, rolling it out the same day in Google Flow Music, with advances in musicality, lyrics, vocals and creative control
key_facts.excerpt: We're launching Lyria 3.5 in Google Flow Music, with advances across musicality, lyrics, vocals, and creative control... We're rolling it out today in Google Flow Music

key_facts.fact: Google lists four improvements: richer melodic structures, higher-quality lyrics with better prompt adherence and structural awareness, more expressive and realistic vocals with improved pronunciation, and easier control over tempo and duration
key_facts.excerpt: Improved musicality... Enhanced lyrics: Generate higher quality lyrics with improved prompt adherence and structural awareness. Improved vocals... Creative control: More easily control the tempo and duration of your outputs.

key_facts.fact: DeepMind describes Lyria 3.5 as its most advanced music generation model, supporting tracks up to three minutes long
key_facts.excerpt: Our most advanced music generation model, now up to 3 minutes long

key_facts.fact: The release adds direct BPM control; Flow Music was built by Riffusion founders Seth Forsgren and Hayk Martiros, whose startup Google acquired earlier this year
key_facts.excerpt: Google shipped Lyria 3.5 to Flow Music on July 29th, putting DeepMind's newest music model inside the AI music studio built by Seth Forsgren and Hayk Martiros before Google acquired their startup earlier this year... The release also adds direct BPM control

key_facts.fact: Google did not say whether Lyria 3.5 replaces Lyria 3 Pro in the Gemini app or developer platforms; Google AI Plus, AI Pro and AI Ultra subscribers get different Flow Music tiers
key_facts.excerpt: Google did not mention whether Lyria 3.5 will replace Lyria 3 Pro across the Gemini app and developer platforms. However, Google AI Plus members get the benefits of Google Flow Music's Starter plan, AI Pro members get the benefits of Google Flow Music's Plus plan, and AI Ultra members get the benefits of Google Flow Music's Member plan.

key_facts.fact: Flow Music already lets users edit specific sections of a track, rewrite or translate lyrics, change instruments and restyle a beat without recreating the whole song
key_facts.excerpt: Google Flow Music—an AI-powered music creation platform with several unique features, such as the ability to edit specific sections of a track, rewrite lyrics, translate them into another language, change instruments, or restyle a beat without modifying the rest of the song.
